claim: FineWeb-Edu contains 1.3 trillion GPT-2 tokens of educational web text, filtered from the ~15T-token FineWeb corpus at a classifier threshold of 3.
stance_target: The repo's data-pipeline claim that a 9B-token training mix can be sourced from an openly released, high-quality web corpus with ample headroom
scope_conditions: FineWeb-Edu v1.4.0, all CC-MAIN dumps 2013-2025, GPT-2 tokenizer
quoted_support: FineWeb-Edu dataset consists of 1.3T tokens and 5.4T tokens (FineWeb-Edu-score-2) of educational web pages filtered from FineWeb dataset. This is the 1.3 trillion version.

claim: Applying the educational classifier to the full 15T-token FineWeb required 6,000 H100 GPU hours, so data curation alone consumes accelerator time comparable to a meaningful fraction of a small training run.
stance_target: The repo's claim that data-pipeline cost must be budgeted separately from training cost on a fixed-compute box
scope_conditions: FineWeb-Edu classifier inference over the 15T-token FineWeb corpus
quoted_support: The classification of FineWeb 15T tokens took 6k H100 GPU hours.

claim: The FineWeb-Edu classifier is a BERT-like regression model fine-tuned on 500k Llama3-70B-Instruct educational-quality annotations on a 0-5 additive scale, achieving F1 82% at a threshold of 3.
stance_target: Whether the repo could reproduce the educational filtering step locally rather than downloading the pre-filtered corpus
scope_conditions: FineWeb-Edu classifier training, 500k annotated FineWeb samples
quoted_support: We fine-tuned a Bert-like regression model using these annotations, based on Snowflake-arctic-embed-m. When converted to a binary classification using a score of 3 as a threshold for keeping and removing files, the model achieved an F1 score of 82%.

claim: The threshold-3 filter removed 92% of FineWeb, which is why the 1.3T-token release is a small fraction of the 15T-token source and why the threshold-2 variant retains 5.4T tokens.
stance_target: How much data a quality filter costs, relevant to whether a small run can afford aggressive filtering
quoted_support: We then built FineWeb-Edu by filtering out samples with scores lower than 3. This removed 92% of the dataset, leaving us with 1.3T educational tokens... we also experimented with a less strict threshold of 2 instead of 3... it preserved 5.4T tokens.

claim: FineWeb-Edu ships nested sample configs of 10BT, 100BT and 350BT GPT-2 tokens, with sample-10BT sampled from sample-100BT which is sampled from sample-350BT.
stance_target: Whether the repo's 9B-token mix can be sourced from a pre-sampled subset without streaming the full 1.3T corpus
quoted_support: sample-350BT: a subset randomly sampled from the whole dataset of around 350B gpt2 tokens; sample-100BT: a subset randomly sampled from the whole dataset of around 100B gpt2 tokens; sample-10BT: a subset randomly sampled from the whole dataset of around 10B gpt2 tokens. sample-10BT was sampled from sample-100BT which in turn was sampled from sample-350BT.

claim: Each FineWeb-Edu record carries a token_count field (observed range 35 to 159k GPT-2 tokens) alongside score and int_score, enabling exact token budgeting without a separate tokenizer pass.
stance_target: The repo's data-pipeline requirement for deterministic token accounting in a 9B-token mix
quoted_support: text stringlengths 150 592k | id string | dump string | url string | date | file_path string | language string | language_score float64 0.65 1 | token_count int64 35 159k | score float64 2.52 5.06 | int_score int64.

claim: FineWeb-Edu is released under the Open Data Commons Attribution License (ODC-By) v1.0 and is additionally subject to CommonCrawl's Terms of Use.
stance_target: Licensing constraints on redistributing or training on the corpus
quoted_support: The dataset is released under the Open Data Commons Attribution License (ODC-By) v1.0 license. The use of this dataset is also subject to CommonCrawl's Terms of Use.

claim: Deduplicating FineWeb-Edu had no measurable impact on model performance in the authors' ablation setup of a 1.8B model trained on 350B tokens, and the deduplicated version is released as a 220B-token subset.
stance_target: The assumption that deduplication is a mandatory quality step for a small-scale run
quoted_support: We find that the deduplication of this dataset doesn't have any impact on model performance in our ablation setup (1.8B trained on 350B tokens).
